function: Uplink power allocation and user scheduling in an integrated satellite and cell-free AP network, learned by a heterogeneous GNN (SHGNN) from channel statistics (p. 2, p. 7, p. 9).
system: NGSO satellite with 5x5 antenna array plus 40 single-antenna APs, single-antenna IoT users; 3 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, p. 9).
method: Heterogeneous GNN (SHGNN) with mean aggregation, MLPs and sigmoid output scaled by Pmax; unsupervised training with negative sum-rate loss; GNN-Stable and GNN-Robust variants (p. 9, p. 12).
data_channel: Own Monte Carlo simulator: Rayleigh ground, Rician satellite links, path-loss formulas, 40 APs in 16 km2; training set size not stated (p. 3, p. 9).
test_conditions: GNN-Stable trained with K = 30 users and tested at K = 20, 30, 40, 50; GNN-Robust trained and tested with the same number of users (p. 12).
baselines: Model-based Algorithm 1 (alternating optimization) against the GNN (Table I); random and equal power allocation against Algorithm 1 only (Fig. 8); no earlier learned method (p. 11, p. 12).
metrics: Per-user and sum throughput (Mbps), percentage of scheduled users, convergence of Algorithm 1, sum throughput and run-time (ms) of GNN versus Algorithm 1 (p. 10, p. 11, p. 12).
complexity: Measured run-time: GNN about 30-36 ms for K = 20-50 versus Algorithm 1 621-5089 ms (Table I); no parameter count or FLOPs (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 3: "follows a Rayleigh fading model" - own Monte Carlo channels: Rayleigh ground and Rician satellite fading with path-loss formulas (p. 9); only the satellite shadow-fading variance cites an overview of 3GPP NTN [36]; no TR 38.811 or TR 38.901 model, public dataset or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "the testing phase is applied for a communication system with a various number of users" - GNN-Stable is trained with K = 30 users and tested with K = 20, 30, 40 and 50.
q3_support: p. 12: "the GNN-Robust is a benchmark with an equal number of users in both of the phases" - the learned benchmark is a variant of the proposed GNN; Algorithm 1 is the only other method compared with the GNN and it is not learned.
q4_support: p. 12: "the two learning-based approaches can predict the solution to problem (29) in the order of milliseconds" - run-times in ms for the GNN and Algorithm 1 are given in Table I.
q5_support: p. 9: "for a system with 40 APs" - simulated system with parameters in Section VI; no link, repository or DOI for code or data anywhere in the paper.
notes: Preprint (arXiv v1). Included because the heterogeneous GNN is a learned method for uplink power allocation, which also defines the scheduled users, in a satellite-terrestrial link; the throughput analysis and Algorithm 1 are model-based (p. 2, p. 7, p. 9). Area 6: transmit-power control for a satellite link. q1: the satellite shadow-fading variance cites an overview of 3GPP NTN [36] (p. 9), but the paper does not say that its channel follows TR 38.811 and everything else is a textbook Rayleigh or Rician model, so not met; the reviewer may confirm. q2: the test at 20, 40 and 50 users uses a network trained with 30 users, without retraining (p. 12). q3: random and equal power allocation (Fig. 8, p. 11) are compared with Algorithm 1, not with the GNN; GNN-Robust is a variant of the same method.
